items.title: SegmentedTabs labels overlap when equal shares cannot hold them
items.evidence: Glass at master: src/components/tabs/styles/segmented.css:61 (display: inline-grid), :63 (grid-auto-columns: 1fr, i.e. minmax(auto, 1fr), so a column never shrinks below its label's min-content), :182 (white-space: nowrap), :183 and :216 (0.625rem / 0.75rem inline padding). Nothing in src/components/tabs sets min-inline-size or flex on .segmented-tab, and useSelectionGroup/useSelectionIndicator write no width on the tabs (git grep). release/11.1.1 changes only the bar radius (segmented.css:80 there: max(var(--radius-bar), calc(var(--control-floor) / 2))). Production's glass rule is the same grid: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/.u-build/out/deploy-lt/assets/index-BrYGhsxy.css `.segmented-tabs{...grid-auto-columns:1fr;grid-auto-flow:column;display:inline-grid...}`. Atlas's override: assets/lazy-filter-C5ln0NIR.css `.cp-drawer__body[data-v-4159c36e] .segmented-tabs{display:flex;inline-size:100%}` and `.cp-drawer__body[data-v-4159c36e] .segmented-tabs>.segmented-tab{flex:1 1 0;min-inline-size:0}` (cp-drawer is not a glass class). The capture m1117-algebra/1440-sci-pane-open.png shows four equal shares filling the pane, which glass's grid does not produce.
items.row: G4 (O-413). Holds. The overlap comes from atlas's filter-drawer stylesheet, which turns the strip into a flex row of equal shares with no minimum. That contradicts the row's 'atlas adds no width rule of its own'. Glass's grid already does what the row expects: when equal shares cannot hold a label, the columns size by content and keep the tab padding between labels. If the labels' summed min-content is wider than the track, the strip overflows its box but never overlaps. Nothing lands in glass. Corrected: the release/11.1.1 radius line is :80, not :78.
items.reply: This one comes from atlas's filter drawer: its stylesheet sets `.cp-drawer__body .segmented-tabs { display: flex }` and `.segmented-tab { flex: 1 1 0; min-inline-size: 0 }`, which forces equal shares with no minimum and lets 'Under 40%' run into its neighbour. Glass's strip is a grid whose columns never shrink below their label. Drop those two declarations (keep `inline-size: 100%` if you want the full width) and the items size by content with the tab padding between labels, on 10.1.2 and 11.1.1 alike.

items.title: CommandDialog passes none of its attributes to its Command
items.evidence: master src/components/command/CommandDialog.vue:8 (inheritAttrs: false), :60-63 (commandProps holds only modelValue and open), :97-101 (Command bound to commandProps alone; no $attrs bind anywhere in the template :66-106). Command.vue:20-25 and :51-57 forward $attrs to reka's ComboboxRoot; Command.vue:63-71 already accepts an array model under multiple, but the declared model type is scalar (src/components/_shared/selection.ts:30, ComboboxValue = SelectionValue | null). types.ts:24-27: CommandDialogProps declares only surface and modelValue beyond DialogProps, so every dialog prop is declared and $attrs holds only what is not the dialog's. release/11.1.1 touches only CommandList.vue in the command folder (git diff master release/11.1.1 -- src/components/command). INBOUND.md:368 O-381(b) 'CommandDialog does not forward attributes to its inner Command, so props such as ignoreFilter cannot reach a palette in a dialog', placed 11.1.2 ('CommandDialog forwards its attributes'); docs/tranches/BL/driver/glass-11.1.1-scope.md:128-130 takes every O-375 to O-388 row into 11.1.2.
items.row: G5 (O-413) is the demo rebuild's O-381(b). Holds. It is booked for 11.1.2 and not built on release/11.1.1. The cure binds $attrs onto the inner Command beside commandProps; it adds no prop and changes no default, so it fits a patch. Its witness takes atlas's: CommandDialog with ignore-filter shows 'Wake County' under 'wkae', and with multiple the emitted model is an array. Note: the array passes at runtime, but the model stays typed as a scalar until Command declares `multiple` (G6, 11.3.0).
items.reply: This is already booked for glass 11.1.2: CommandDialog will pass every attribute that is not the dialog's own to its Command, so `ignore-filter` and `multiple` reach the palette in the dialog. Your Dialog + DialogContent + Command composition is the right bridge until then.

items.title: A Command row shows no chosen state under multiple
items.evidence: master src/components/command/CommandItem.vue:39-50 renders RekaComboboxItem with the slot alone, and :46 calls rowClass() with its default 'none'. src/components/_shared/menu/rowClass.ts:19 and :27-30 already define the 'start' arm (ps-7, a 28 px gutter) that SelectItem uses (SelectItem.vue:66 rowClass(indicator), :75-82 the gutter span with RekaSelectItemIndicator). DropdownMenuCheckboxItem.vue:50-54 reserves menu__indicator with a Check glyph. Command.vue:20-24 and :51-57: multiple reaches reka only through $attrs; types.ts:6-17 CommandProps declares neither multiple nor ignoreFilter; the model type is scalar (_shared/selection.ts:30). reka-ui 2.10.1 ships ComboboxItemIndicator (node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Combobox/ComboboxItemIndicator.js), and nothing in src uses it (git grep finds only the Select and menu indicators). release/11.1.1 does not touch CommandItem. Related ruling: glass-11.1.1-scope.md:136-138 (O-393, 11.1.2): in a group with leading icons the check moves to the trailing slot.
items.row: G6 (O-413). Holds. It is shown in glass alone, and no booked row covers a Command row's chosen mark (O-393 and O-414 G17 are menu rows). A visible mark under multiple changes how existing multi-select rows look, and declaring `multiple` and `ignoreFilter` adds props (with `multiple` the model type widens to an array), so this is a minor. It is not dock or Metric work, so it goes to 11.3.0. Build: under multiple, CommandItem takes rowClass('start') and wraps a Check in ComboboxItemIndicator, so the column is reserved when the row is not chosen and labels do not shift. The check's placement follows O-393 (trailing when the group carries leading icons). Corrected cites: SelectItem.vue:66 and :75-82, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem.vue:50-54; 'unused' refers to ComboboxItemIndicator alone.
items.reply: Taken for glass 11.3.0: under `multiple`, a CommandItem gets the same check the menu rows carry, with its column reserved when the row is not chosen, so labels stay put. It follows 11.1.2's rule that the check sits in a trailing column when the group has icons. Command will also declare `multiple` and `ignoreFilter` as props, with an array model under `multiple`. Your chips and 'Chosen' heading are a good interim.

items.title: The Command field's text is 14 px on a phone
items.evidence: Glass at master: src/components/command/styles.css:60 (.command__input font-size: var(--dropdown-text)); src/styles/tokens/sizing.css:76 (--dropdown-text: var(--control-text)); src/styles/tokens/light-dark.css:17-37, :34 (under pointer: coarse, --control-text: max(var(--type-small), 1rem), so 16 px or more since 11.1.0). At v10.1.2 the coarse block sets --ui-scale: var(--ui-coarse-scale, 1.5) (light-dark.css:19 at that tag) and sizing.css:35 there makes control-text = type-small × 1.5, about 21 px. Atlas production: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/.u-build/out/deploy-lt/index.html has <style id="critical-css"> (byte 7779) after both <link>s to assets/index-BrYGhsxy.css (7444, 7557). Inside @layer atlas.recipes it repeats glass's :root tokens ('--ui-scale:1;--ui-coarse-scale:1.5;--control-floor:0px;...--control-text:calc(var(--type-small) * var(--ui-scale))') with no pointer:coarse block, and no script removes it. The main sheet's coarse rule (@media(pointer:coarse){:root{--ui-scale:var(--ui-coarse-scale,1.5);--control-floor:...}}) sits in the same atlas.recipes layer and loses on order. Measured values agree: 14 px is --type-small's floor at 390 with scale 1 (src/styles/typography/scale.css:104-108: clamp(0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.25vw, 1.25rem), 16.4 px at 1440), and arrive-phone.json reads the input at 44 px, the production branch's --control-h-lg at scale 1. The field floor: --field-text-floor is declared at sizing.css:43-49 (0 on a fine pointer, 1rem coarse at light-dark.css:36) and read by control-surfaces.css:58, utilities/components.css:62 and _shared/field/control.css:125, not by .command__input.
items.row: G7 (O-413) is O-350(8) again. O-352 answered it as already true on 11.1.0 through --control-text, and glass-11.1.1-scope.md:96 keeps one computed-style cell to confirm it in 11.1.2; atlas's witness joins that cell. Holds as the consumer's: on glass's own line the palette field is 16 px or more on a coarse pointer (about 21 px on 10.1.2, max(type-small, 16 px) since 11.1.0). Atlas's critical-CSS copy of glass's :root tokens resets the coarse scale and the 44 px control floor on every touch device, so the field reads 14 px; on 11.1.x the same copy would also reset --control-text and --field-text-floor. Nothing lands in glass. A small hardening for that 11.1.2 cell: .command__input does not take max(<rung>, var(--field-text-floor)) as the three field recipes do, so a host that lowers --dropdown-text drops the palette field under 16 px on touch. Corrected: the floor's readers are control-surfaces.css:58, utilities/components.css:62 and _shared/field/control.css:125, not sizing.css:63-68.
items.reply: Glass already floors this field on a touch screen: it reads `--control-text`, which is the small type size × 1.5 on 10.1.2 and at least 16 px since 11.1.0. The 14 px comes from atlas's inlined critical CSS (`<style id="critical-css">` in index.html). It repeats glass's `:root` tokens (`--ui-scale: 1`, `--control-floor: 0px` and the rest) in the same layer after the main sheet, but without glass's `@media (pointer: coarse)` block, so on a phone it also undoes the 44 px touch floor of every glass control. Carry the coarse block into the critical copy, or leave the tokens out of it, and the field reads 16 px or more.

items.title: CommandDialog changes height in one frame as its list narrows
items.evidence: master src/components/command/styles.css:76-92 (.command__list has only max-height: var(--overlay-max-block), no block-size floor and no transition), :16-19 (.command-dialog__content sets only overflow and padding); src/components/dialog/styles.css has no block-size on the plate (its only block-size, :108, is the close control); src/styles/tokens/offsets.css:81 (--overlay-max-block: min(24rem, 60dvh)). release/11.1.1 changes CommandList.vue only to force-mount the list while its dialog closes (git diff master release/11.1.1), not its height while open. Booked: docs/tranches/BL/audit/animation/AUDIT.md:127 (rule G, 'Nothing inside a surface tweens its size ... the command list (up to 195 px a key)') and :192 (row 16, 'Command list | content arrives, leaves or changes size | lands whole and moves what is below it', placed 'W-B.17 (11.2.0, and held)'); INBOUND.md:307 O-332(2) (the same command list, 'W-B.17 (11.2.0, and held for the size pieces)'); docs/tranches/BL/waves/W-B.17.md:505 ('the command list in its dialog; a dialog or sheet whose content changes | resizes in one frame | one follow() on the surface; its rows fade'), :23 ('Held, 11.2.0 or later, each behind one reading'), :399-404 (ship conditions that name CommandDialog: longest layout 0.94 ms or under at 4x in Chromium, no more than one frame in ten over 20 ms in WebKit, rows fade), :406 (a reserved-footprint fallback is a changed default, a 12.0.0 row).
items.row: G8 (O-413). Corrected from 'a new 11.1.2 defect row; no INBOUND row books it'. The animation audit measured this exact step (the command list, up to 195 px a key), and W-B.17 books the cure: one follow() on the dialog, its rows fading, held behind a layout-cost reading that names CommandDialog. The seat's proposed cure, a block-size tween measured from ResizeObserver entries, still lays out on every frame of the tween, which is the cost the hold exists for, so it cannot skip that reading. Release: where the booked row sits, 11.2.0 or later, shipped when its reading passes. O-379(a) moved LabeledField's error line, another held follow site, into 11.1.2. The palette could ride 11.1.2 the same way only if its reading passes before that cut. A fixed block size would change resting looks and is W-B.17's 12.0.0 fallback, not taken. Atlas's frames (motion-desk.json, motion-phone.json: 406 to 217 to 173 px; 407, 225, 175 at 390) join the row's witnesses: no height step larger than the tween's per-frame share, both engines.
items.reply: This is already on glass's list: the palette resizing in one frame as its list narrows is one of the size changes glass's motion work will tween (the dialog follows its list's height and the rows fade). It is planned for 11.2.0 or the release after, once its per-frame layout cost in CommandDialog measures within budget. Your fixed-height search dialog doesn't need to wait for it.

items.title: The dock's search field re-ranks and drops a source's rows
items.evidence: master src/components/dock/composables/useDockSearch.ts:162-164 (an onSearch source only fills the matcher's items), :181-186 (every row passes through useFuzzySearch), :194-220 (the async adapter); src/composables/search/match.ts:44-94 (subsequence scorer, null when a token is not a subsequence, :89), :149-175 (label 12, type 10, text 3). The matcher is internal, not exported: src/composables/search/index.ts:3-9 (no ./search export key), scripts/lib/subpath-policy.mjs:145 (search: "INTERNAL"); git grep finds no caller in src outside useDockSearch, whose public door is src/components/dock/index.ts:105. The dock redesign removes the helper: docs/tranches/BL/design/dock/wi8/RULINGS-6.md:159 and :293 (REMOVES: useDockSearch, its two types, the #search slot and search.css, 'gaggle and atlas both built search in other slots'), RULINGS-6.md:334 and RULINGS-7.md:517 (owner question 12, default: delete in 11.2.0), RULINGS-7.md:194 (useDockSearch among the step-2 deletions).
items.row: G9 (O-413), an ask. The verdict holds, and one premise is corrected. The cause is read correctly: a source's rows are re-scored and filtered by the subsequence matcher. The redesign deletes useDockSearch and the #search slot because no site used them, and atlas's plan is the first named use, so whether the helper stays is owner question 12. Default offered: delete as ruled. Atlas's search stays a CommandDialog, where its own ranker sets the order through ignore-filter once O-381(b) ships in 11.1.2. If the owner keeps the helper, both of atlas's options land with the 11.2.0 dock work as options on the helper: keep a ranked source's order and drop none, or better tiers in the matcher. Corrected: the matcher is not exported (search/index.ts:3-9), so its tiers reach no consumer except through this helper. The seat's line 'word-start tiers in the exported matcher would change every consumer's ranking, a minor (11.3.0)' does not stand, and that option falls with the owner's answer. Note for the owner question: this placement's release rule puts a removal in 12.0.0, while the redesign's default deletes in 11.2.0; question 12 should settle the version too.
items.reply: Glass's dock search helper is due to be removed in 11.2.0, because no site had used it. Now that we have your plan, we're asking the owner whether it stays; our default is that it goes. If it stays, an option to keep your source's order and drop nothing comes with it in 11.2.0. Either way, your own ranker can drive a CommandDialog with `ignore-filter` once 11.1.2 forwards it, so 'wkae' finds Wake County in your order.

items.title: Hover cards, notes, menus and selects are opaque paper with no blur
items.evidence: `git show d46646127` (2026-11-05, 'the subtle register', design pass 2) adds --glass-chrome-paper: 86% and paints floating and overlay surfaces as card paper over the veil, with floating blur 6px and saturate 1.05; af72d79a3, dd74bf23a, d3d525806 ('opaque chrome register') and 64f5f2483 follow. None is an ancestor of master or release/11.1.1 (git merge-base --is-ancestor); they sit on atlas's u/* glass branches (u/b7-glass, u/dp-integ-glass, u/dp2-glass to u/dp6-glass, u/fl-G1, u/fl-G2, u/fl-RG, u/sp-integ-glass and others), and d46646127 is an ancestor of 8b4d8f82b, atlas's production glass. The merge base of 8b4d8f82b with master is 373ed8aba (2026-11-04). Master: src/styles/tokens/glass.css:72 (--glass-blur-floating-radius: 20px), :91 (--glass-blur-floating: blur(20px × level) saturate(1.5)); --glass-level is 1 by default (src/styles/tokens/property-regs.css:154-158); src/styles/glass/ladder.css:124-144 (.glass-floating: veil plate @apply glass-plate :133, backdrop-filter :138, rim and shadows :141-144). --glass-chrome-paper does not exist on master. release/11.1.1 ca17dd857 'a phone popup is glass': src/styles/glass/surface-axis.css:99-114 there ([data-plate=firm]: overlay veil tier, --glass-level 0.35, so 22 px × 0.35 = 7.7 px of blur per glass.css:73 and :92 there; solid under reduced transparency), worn by the phone Select and the dock DropdownMenu. Booked, not covered by the seat: docs/tranches/BL/driver/glass-11.1.1-scope.md:87 (11.1.2: 'a floor on the Popover and menu plate's opacity (fourier 13, C-21)'), INBOUND.md:316-317 (O-292a row 13, 'a floor on the Popover and menu plate's opacity so text behind never reads', with O-297a C-21).
items.row: G10 (O-413). The verdict and release hold, and a booked row was missing. The opaque paper atlas sees comes from its own glass branch's design passes, which glass's released line never took. On glass's line, floating surfaces are 20 px veils (the 2026-11-06 look); adopting 11.1.1 brings those back, plus the firm glass phone menus and selects (ca17dd857). The legibility half of the ask is already booked for 11.1.2: O-292a row 13 with O-297a C-21 puts a floor under the popover and menu plate's opacity so text behind never reads. The rest is a bounded readout look (blur at or under 6 px, paper below 100 %, rim and shadow kept, 4.5:1 over a saturated field). It settles two owner orders ('less blur' of 11-05, 'more frost and glass veil' of 11-17 and 11-18), so it is the owner's. Default offered: open 11.1.1's firm plate as a declared option for hover cards, popovers, menus and selects in 11.3.0, keeping the floating veil the default, with witnesses over the /sci district map in both engines. The owner should know the firm plate blurs about 7.7 px, above atlas's 6 px bound. Related, not duplicates: O-404 (a site override that makes a surface opaque is the site's), O-414 G5 and G6, and LF-15 (the dialog veil, 11.3.0). It is not dock or Metric work, so it is not 11.2.0.
items.reply: The opaque paper on production comes from the design-pass commits on atlas's own glass branch (d46646127 among them), which never reached glass's released line. In 11.1.1, hover cards, popovers and menus are veils with a 20 px blur, phone menus and selects wear a firmer veil that holds 4.5:1, and 11.1.2 adds a floor under the popover and menu plate's opacity so text behind never reads through. A bounded readout plate for content over figures is a look we're putting to the owner. The default we'd offer is that firmer veil (about 8 px of blur) as an opt-in for hover cards, popovers, menus and selects in glass 11.3.0.

items.title: A tooltip opens on a scripted focus and stays
items.evidence: master src/components/tooltip/Tooltip.vue:4-12 and :29-36 (only open, defaultOpen, delayDuration and disabled reach reka's TooltipRoot; inheritAttrs false with no $attrs bind, :18); src/components/tooltip/TooltipProvider.vue:4-9 and :21-24 (only delayDuration and skipDelayDuration). reka-ui 2.10.1 supports the guard: node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Tooltip/TooltipRoot.js:44 and :60 (ignoreNonKeyboardFocus, inherited from the provider), TooltipTrigger.js:72 (with it set, a focus that does not match :focus-visible does not open). The scripted focus: src/components/dock/GlassDock.vue:340-357 (when the dock folds with focus inside, it focuses the first persistent control, target.focus() at :356). No dock part wraps its own tooltip root (git grep TooltipRoot over src), so a cure in Tooltip and TooltipProvider reaches a consumer's `<Tooltip>` around a dock control. release/11.1.1 changes only TooltipContent.vue (the leave-finished event), not the trigger's focus rule. Booked: INBOUND.md:329 O-350(9) 'Tooltip opens on programmatic focus return and under a resting pointer'; docs/tranches/BL/driver/glass-11.1.1-scope.md:96 (11.1.2: 'a Tooltip opens on a pointer move or keyboard focus only, never on programmatic focus return or under a resting pointer'); the exits scope (glass-11.1.1-exits-scope.md:5, :16, :18) took only O-350's exit and reduced-motion rows.
items.row: G13 (O-413) is O-350(9). Holds. It was first placed for 11.1.1, but the exits patch did not build it, and it sits in 11.1.2's scope. The cure sets reka's ignoreNonKeyboardFocus inside glass's Tooltip by default. Consumers cannot set that option today, so no consumer chose it and the change fits a patch. The dock's focus hand-off after a pick then opens no label, while Tab still does. Atlas's witness joins the row's: element.focus() after a pointer press shows no tooltip; Tab shows it. Exposing ignoreNonKeyboardFocus and disableHoverableContent as props would add props, a minor (11.3.0), taken only if atlas still needs them after the default changes.
items.reply: This is already booked for glass 11.1.2: glass's Tooltip will open only on a pointer move or keyboard focus, never on a scripted focus such as the dock's hand-off after a pick. So after your step no label shows, and a Tab to the crest still shows 'Home', with no props needed. Exposing `ignoreNonKeyboardFocus` and `disableHoverableContent` as props would come in 11.3.0 if you still need them after that.
